Bill.BriefDescription: Encouraging middle and junior high schools to address the issue of eating disorders in their health and fitness curriculum.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to instructing students about eating disorders; andadding a new section to chapter 28A.230 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 28A.230RCW to read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The legislature finds that as many as twentyfour millionpeople in the United States suffer from an eating disorder, and ninetyfive percent of those individuals are between the ages of twelve andtwentyfive. Even more disturbing is that anorexia is the third mostcommon chronic illness among adolescents, and more people die of eatingdisorders than any other mental illness. Fortunately, eating disordersare preventable and can be treated. However, early intervention is thekey to successful prevention and treatment. It is essential thatmiddle and junior high school children are taught the physical dangersof eating disorders in order to dismiss the glamorization of being toothin that occurs in the media. Including instruction about eatingdisorders in the middle and junior high school classroom alsoencourages teachers to become better educated and to recognize the p. 1 HB 3291warning symptoms and appropriate intervention if a student shows earlysigns of an eating disorder. (2) All public middle and junior high schools in the state arestrongly encouraged to ensure that instruction is provided to studentsin the health and fitness curriculum regarding identification of thewarning signs, behavioral patterns, and avenues of support for youngpeople with abnormal eating behaviors or eating disorders.
